title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: contract rating, customer tenure and waiting periods by category
content:
## What this card covers
This card sets out, for each acceptance category of the Dangerous Goods Acceptance product, the applicant- and booking-side parameters: whether the booking must be rated under a service contract, the minimum age of the customer profile, the length of the misdeclaration block, and the waiting period after a rejection before a new application for the same booking is accepted.

## Parameters by category
| Category | Booking must be contract-rated | Minimum profile age (calendar days) | Misdeclaration block (calendar days) | Wait after rejection (calendar days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AHL DG Limited Quantity | No | 0 | 180 | 0 |
| AHL DG Class 9 Standard | No | 0 | 180 | 0 |
| AHL DG Flammables and Corrosives | No | 0 | 365 | 1 |
| AHL DG Toxics and Oxidizers | No | 90 | 365 | 2 |
| AHL DG Compressed Gases | Yes | 90 | 365 | 2 |
| AHL DG Special Approval | Yes | 365 | 730 | 7 |

## What each column means
- **Contract-rated booking**: "Yes" means the booking carrying the goods must be rated under a service contract.
- **Minimum profile age**: the number of calendar days the customer profile must have existed; 0 sets no minimum.
- **Misdeclaration block**: the number of calendar days after a misdeclaration penalty during which the customer's new applications for the category are refused.
- **Wait after rejection**: the number of calendar days after a rejection before a new application for the same booking is accepted; 0 sets no waiting period.

## Basis Q&A
- *Which categories require a contract-rated booking?* AHL DG Compressed Gases and AHL DG Special Approval.
- *Which category has the longest misdeclaration block?* AHL DG Special Approval, at 730 calendar days.
- *Does AHL DG Class 9 Standard impose a minimum profile age?* No; its figure is 0.
